question: Which statement correctly distinguishes somatic death from cellular death?

answers.text: Somatic death and cellular death occur simultaneously at the moment the heart stops

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. These are sequential, not simultaneous. Somatic (clinical) death precedes cellular death. After somatic death, individual cells continue to survive for minutes to hours depending on their oxygen requirements.

answers.text: Somatic death is the irreversible cessation of integrated vital functions; cellular death follows as individual cells lose function over the subsequent minutes to hours

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Somatic death is defined as the irreversible cessation of the three integrated vital functions: cardiovascular, respiratory, and neurological. Cellular death is the subsequent progressive loss of individual cell function, with cells dying at different rates based on oxygen sensitivity (neurons within minutes, corneal cells within hours).

answers.text: Cellular death refers only to brain cell death, which triggers somatic death

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Cellular death refers to the loss of function of all individual cells throughout the body, not just brain cells. Moreover, somatic death is not caused by cellular death — it is the other way around.

answers.text: Somatic death is reversible with CPR; cellular death is not

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. By definition, somatic death is irreversible. CPR may reverse clinical cardiac arrest before somatic death is established — but somatic death itself is defined as irreversible cessation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Somatic death is the irreversible cessation of integrated vital functions (heart, breathing, brain). Cellular death follows — individual cells survive for varying periods. This distinction is critical for organ donation.
Correct. Remember: somatic death (integrated function ceases, irreversible) precedes cellular death (individual cells die progressively). This sequence underlies organ donation timelines.
